title: Completion report lock UI — locked state display + admin unlock button
tech: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, CSS Modules, Axios
keyConstraints: TypeScript strict mode, no UI component libraries, CSS Modules only, no localStorage or sessionStorage
description: When a completion report has been approved (approvedAt is set), the UI must clearly show it is locked and prevent re-submission. Admins see an Unlock button that calls the unlock endpoint and re-enables editing. Drivers and Dispatchers see a locked notice only — no unlock option.
acceptanceCriteria: CompletionModal shows a locked banner (e.g. 'Approved — locked for editing') and disables the submit button when job.completionReport.approvedAt is not null
Admin role sees an Unlock button inside the locked banner; clicking it calls POST /api/jobs/:id/completion-report/unlock via axiosInstance and reloads the completion report state on success
Unlock button shows a loading state while the request is in flight and displays the error message from the API response on failure
After successful unlock, the locked banner disappears and the completion report form becomes editable again without a full page reload
npx tsc --noEmit passes with no errors
implementationNotes: Do not rewrite working code — only add what is missing.
CSS Modules only — no inline styles.
Read approvedAt from job.completionReport.approvedAt (already returned by jobInclude on the backend).
Use AuthContext to get current user role for the Admin-only Unlock button conditional render.
Use axiosInstance from api/axios.ts for the unlock API call.
Locked banner should be visually distinct — use a warning/amber color class in the CSS module, not a generic info style.
Unlock button label: 'Unlock for editing'. Confirm dialog is optional — keep it simple for v1.
After unlock success, update local state to set completionReport.approvedAt = null so the UI reacts without refetching the full job.
securityConsiderations: The Unlock button must only render for Admin role — check via AuthContext. The backend enforces the real security; this is UX-only protection.
